t: Section 130 of the Truth in Lending Act (15 U.S.C. 1640) is amended by adding after subsection (k) (as added by this title) the following new subsection:“(l) Exemption From Liability and Rescission in Case of Borrower Fraud or Deception.—In addition to any other remedy available by law or contract, no creditor or assignee shall be liable to an obligor under this section, if such obligor, or co-obligor has been convicted of obtaining by actual fraud such residential mortgage loan.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a provision about civil liability and remedies involves a right to sue, but the liability here runs between private creditors and borrowers, not against a federal decision. The section only exempts creditors from liability where the borrower was convicted of fraud. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking, or right to challenge a federal action.
fable.s: no creditor or assignee shall be liable to an obligor under this section, if such obligor, or co-obligor has been convicted of obtaining by actual fraud such residential mortgage loan

qwen_block.w: This section defines a legal exemption from liability for creditors in cases of borrower fraud. It does not involve any process where the federal government consults with or coordinates with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The interaction described is between private parties (creditors and obligors) regarding legal liability, not federal decision-making.
qwen_block.s: no creditor or assignee shall be liable to an obligor under this section, if such obligor, or co-obligor has been convicted of obtaining by actual fraud such residential mortgage loan.

opus.w: This section creates an exemption from civil liability in private suits between borrowers and creditors or assignees. It does not involve any federal decision or let outside parties take part in one. The litigation it mentions is private-party liability, not a right to sue or object to a federal decision. It also limits a remedy rather than granting one.
opus.s: no creditor or assignee shall be liable to an obligor under this section, if such obligor, or co-obligor has been convicted of obtaining by actual fraud such residential mortgage loan.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** It's tempting to read this as participation because it deals with liability and lawsuits under the Truth in Lending Act. That reading fails because the liability here is between private parties: borrowers (obligors) suing creditors or assignees. No federal decision is involved, and no outside party gets a right to sue or object to the government. The section only narrows a private right of action when the borrower was convicted of fraud.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a condition under which creditors are exempt from liability (if the borrower was convicted of fraud). It does not require the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from any outside party (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The reference to a criminal conviction is a factual predicate for liability, not a participatory mechanism.
qwen_chat.s: no creditor or assignee shall be liable to an obligor under this section, if such obligor, or co-obligor has been convicted of obtaining by actual fraud such residential mortgage loan
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "convicted of obtaining by actual fraud" implies a legal process involving the public (the borrower), and thus constitutes participation. However, this is merely a condition for liability exemption based on a prior criminal conviction, not a procedural requirement for the government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties before making a decision. The section defines a legal standard for liability, not a participatory process.
